_about: Records that should, did or may exist but are not held: one deduped list (existing MR/EV ids reused; new items MR-0069 to MR-0083). Each new record carries the record, a neutral description and a separately labelled interpretation. Sketches are pencil reconstructions captioned "tab.bot artist reconstruction"; they show no real document. Sketches for existing records are proposed in catalogue-change PRs. Built 6 Nov 2026 — Tab agent

new_records.title: Survey and valuation of Llandough manor, 1824 (Bute estate papers)
new_records.expected_holder: National Library of Wales (Bute papers, entry "LLANDOUGH MANOR, survey and valuation, with other manors")
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: The National Library of Wales catalogue of the Bute papers lists a survey and valuation of Llandough manor with other manors. A manorial survey of that date would list each holding, its occupier and its value. No copy has been seen.
new_records.source: NLW Bute papers catalogue entry; map-1824 research report; related plan EV-0211 (Glamorgan Archives DB/E/1 plan 19, partly held)
new_records.description: A bound or loose estate survey of 1824 listing the holdings in Llandough manor with acreages, occupiers and valuations, probably with a reference plan.
new_records.interpretation: If it survives, the survey would show how the Tŷ Mawr holding was described and valued in 1824, and could be read against the 1824 plan already partly held.
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction

new_records.title: HM Land Registry first-registration application and application plan, title WA231076 (1982)
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: Title WA231076 was first registered on an application lodged in 1982. A first-registration application is made on a prescribed form with the deeds and a plan identifying the land. The register is held; the application form and its plan are not.
new_records.source: Title register WA231076; related records MR-0020 (Form A13 and requisitions), EV-0059, EV-0063
new_records.description: A Land Registry application form of 1982 with an attached plan marking the land applied for, lodged with the title deeds relied on.
new_records.interpretation: The application plan would show exactly which land was claimed in 1982 and how it was drawn, before the titles were merged in 1987.
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction

new_records.title: South Wales Police internal review 1188/26 (of FOI 719/26): outcome document
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: The force sent its internal-review response on time on 26 October 2026 as a password-protected PDF. No password was sent, so the content has not been read.
new_records.source: Email from South Wales Police, 26 October 2026 (email ingest)
new_records.description: A police information-rights letter giving the outcome of an internal review of an earlier freedom of information request.
new_records.interpretation: Until it can be opened, it is not known whether the review released more material or upheld the original response.
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction

new_records.title: Llandough Community Council: original and revised agendas for the meeting of 22 October 2026, with publication dates
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: The council's reply (item 5) states the agenda "was amended in good time to provide for the three clear day's notice". An amended agenda implies an earlier version and a date for each publication. Neither version with its date is held.
new_records.source: Llandough Community Council reply, October 2026, item 5 (email ingest cycle 27 Oct 2026)
new_records.description: Two versions of a one-page parish meeting agenda, each with a date of publication.
new_records.interpretation: The two versions, with their dates, would show what was added or changed and whether notice rules were met.
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction

new_records.title: Llandough Community Council: record of the decision to hold the 22 October 2026 meeting remotely
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: The meeting was held remotely. A council decision on the form of a meeting would normally be recorded with who made it, when and under what authority. No such record has been supplied.
new_records.source: Llandough Community Council correspondence, October 2026 (email ingest cycle 27 Oct 2026)
new_records.description: A short minute, email or clerk's note recording who decided the meeting would be remote and on what date.
new_records.interpretation: The record would show whether the decision was taken by the council, a chair or the clerk, and under which standing order.
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction

new_records.title: Llandough Community Council records about Tŷ Mawr / Great House Farm beyond the minute books deposited in 2002
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: The council's reply (item 2) describes its holdings as "Uncertain at this stage pending the outcome of the internal review". Correspondence and files outside the deposited minute books would normally be kept by the clerk.
new_records.source: Llandough Community Council reply, October 2026, items 2 and 8
new_records.description: Clerk's correspondence files and papers about the farm, kept separately from the minute books deposited at the record office in 2002.
new_records.interpretation: Such files could hold letters to and from the council about the farm that the minutes only summarise.
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction

new_records.title: Known signatures of John Williams of Great House Farm (born c.1867), c.1911–1950
new_records.expected_holder: The National Archives (census RG 14 / RG 15; National Farm Survey MAF 32); Probate Service; estate papers
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: A householder signed the 1911 and 1921 census schedules. A 1916 tenancy counterpart (MR-0003) and the 1949 surrender papers (MR-0007) would carry his signature, as would a will if one was made.
new_records.source: Legal ticklist row T28; MR-0003; MR-0007; MR-0047
new_records.description: Census household schedules and other documents of 1911–1950 bearing the signature of the farm's tenant.
new_records.interpretation: A set of known signatures would allow a handwriting comparison with the signature on the May 1939 agreement (EV-0023).
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction

new_records.title: Bank staff record for the attesting witness to the May 1939 agreement
new_records.expected_holder: Lloyds Banking Group Archives (whether 1939 staff registers survive: not checked)
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: The May 1939 agreement (EV-0023) is witnessed by a person described as a cashier at Lloyds Bank; the reading of the name is uncertain. Banks kept staff registers.
new_records.description: A bank staff register or service card for a branch cashier employed in 1939.
new_records.interpretation: A staff record would confirm whether the witness was a real local cashier at the stated date.
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction

new_records.title: Petition for leave to appeal to the House of Lords, 1987 (Parliamentary Archives HL/PO/JO/10/11/2536 item 19)
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: The Court of Appeal order refused leave and granted a stay pending a petition. The Parliamentary Archives catalogue lists the item. It has not been read.
new_records.source: Court of Appeal order, 1987; Parliamentary Archives catalogue HL/PO/JO/10/11/2536 item 19; legal ticklist row T25
new_records.description: A printed or typed petition to the House of Lords Appeal Committee seeking leave to appeal a 1987 Court of Appeal decision.
new_records.interpretation: The petition would show which grounds were put forward in 1987, including whether dishonesty was raised before 1989.
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction

new_records.title: Court of Appeal registry papers for the notice of appeal of 30 October 1974
new_records.expected_holder: Civil Appeals Office; The National Archives (J series) — not checked
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: The Court of Appeal judgment records that a notice of appeal was issued on 30 October 1974. Appeal registry records may survive separately from the county court file, which Cardiff County Court no longer holds (MR-0012, MR-0014).
new_records.source: Court of Appeal judgment (1987); legal ticklist rows T08; MR-0012; MR-0014
new_records.description: A court registry file or entry book recording an appeal lodged in October 1974, with the notice of appeal.
new_records.interpretation: The registry papers could supply the 1974 grounds of appeal that the lost county court file would otherwise have held.
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction

new_records.title: Contract or memorandum of sale, BP Pension Trust Ltd to BP Properties Ltd, on or before 31 October 1974 (farmhouse and garden)
new_records.expected_holder: BP group legal records; solicitors acting in 1974–75
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: The farmhouse and garden were conveyed in May 1975 (MR-0050). A sale between companies is usually preceded by a contract, and the 31 October 1974 letters suggest the arrangement predated them.
new_records.description: A short contract between two group companies agreeing the sale of a farmhouse and garden, signed for each company.
new_records.interpretation: Its date would fix when the transfer was agreed relative to the October 1974 letters.
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction

new_records.title: Written rejection of the 31 October 1974 letters by Mary (Nancy) Williams or her solicitors (November 1974 – March 1983)
new_records.expected_holder: BP group records; solicitors acting for either side
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: If the offer in the 31 October 1974 letters was declined, a reply would normally be in writing and kept on the recipient's file. None has been produced.
new_records.description: A solicitor's letter or handwritten reply declining the terms set out in October 1974.
new_records.interpretation: Its existence or absence bears on whether the 1974 offer was refused or left unanswered.
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction

new_records.title: ITV/HTV Report Wales film items on the Llandough cottage protests, 11 April and 1 November 1974 (CAN 2775 item 4; CAN 2904 item 8)
new_records.expected_holder: National Library of Wales (National Screen and Sound Archive)
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: The film catalogue lists both items. The underlying film or preservation copies were requested under FOI/2026/15; a reply is due 25 November 2026.
new_records.description: Two short regional television news films from 1974 held as film cans or preservation copies.
new_records.interpretation: The footage would show the farmhouse and the protests as filmed in 1974.
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction

new_records.title: GGAT 1989–90 consultee and evaluation file for Great House Farm (incl. 1990 evaluation, S387 file, 1 Oct 1982 letter)
new_records.expected_holder: Heneb (holds the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust records)
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: The trust commented as consultee on outline application 89/01396/OUT and carried out an evaluation in 1990. The complaint of 28 October 2026 closed without a search or a not-held statement.
new_records.source: Heneb complaint outcome, 28 October 2026 (email ingest cycle 29 Oct 2026)
new_records.description: An archaeological trust project file with consultee letters, an evaluation report and site notes.
new_records.interpretation: The file would show what the trust recorded about the farmhouse when development was proposed.
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction

new_records.title: Owner/occupier notification lists for SSSI 0524, 1972 and 1985
new_records.expected_holder: Natural Resources Wales (successor to the Nature Conservancy Council)
new_records.why_we_believe_it_exists: Notification of a Site of Special Scientific Interest is served on each owner and occupier, and a list of those served is kept. Requested under EIR CAS-322825-L6S1; response due 17 November 2026.
new_records.source: NRW EIR CAS-322825-L6S1 acknowledgement (email ingest cycle 27 Oct 2026)
new_records.description: Typed schedules of the owners and occupiers served with notice of the site designation in 1972 and 1985.
new_records.interpretation: The lists would show whom the authority treated as owner and occupier of the land at each date.
new_records.caption: tab.bot artist reconstruction
